data.name: GetStartedDescription
data.value: Customize your workspace, learn the basics, and connect your first device.

data.name: ChooseThemeDescription
data.value: Choose a theme for your workspace. Open Themes, edit a theme, enable it and save. When several themes are enabled, the theme with the highest priority is used.

data.name: BasicSettingsDescription
data.value: Choose your language and time zone in your user settings. Save your changes to apply them to your account.

data.name: ApplicationSettingsDescription
data.value: Review the server settings and configure the options needed for your installation.

data.name: FundamentalsDescription
data.value: Follow these steps to connect an agent, prepare device templates, add devices, and schedule their operations.

data.name: FundamentalsAgentTitle
data.value: 1. Download an agent and create a PAT

data.name: FundamentalsAgentDescription
data.value: The agent connects Gurux.DLMS.AMI to your devices. It authenticates to the server with a personal access token (PAT).

data.name: FundamentalsAgentDownload
data.value: Open Configure your account and select Download the agent. Install it on a computer that can reach your devices.

data.name: FundamentalsAgentToken
data.value: On the same page, enter a token name and expiration time, then generate an access token. Copy the token when it is displayed.

data.name: FundamentalsAgentConfigure
data.value: Configure the agent with your AMI server address and the token, then start it. Open Agents to check that it has connected. You can review or revoke tokens in your user settings.

data.name: FundamentalsImportTitle
data.value: 2. Import manufacturer settings or a custom device template

data.name: FundamentalsImportDescription
data.value: Prepare the device settings before adding a device. Use manufacturer settings or import your own Gurux device template.

data.name: FundamentalsManufacturerImport
data.value: Open Manufacturers, check for available settings, select the manufacturer settings you need, and choose Install.

data.name: FundamentalsTemplateImport
data.value: To use a custom template, open Add device template, select a .gxc file exported from Gurux.DLMS.Director, review the settings, give the template a name, and save it.

data.name: FundamentalsTemplateTitle
data.value: 3. Create a device from a device template

data.name: FundamentalsTemplateDescription
data.value: A device template supplies the protocol settings and objects for a device.

data.name: FundamentalsTemplateSelect
data.value: Open Add device and select the manufacturer, model, version and device settings, or choose a custom device template.

data.name: FundamentalsTemplateConnection
data.value: Give the device a name and choose the agent and connection settings needed to reach it.

data.name: FundamentalsTemplateSave
data.value: Review the settings inherited from the template and save the device.

data.name: FundamentalsDeviceDescription
data.value: Configure each device with its own connection details and credentials, even when several devices share a template.

data.name: FundamentalsDeviceSettings
data.value: Open Add device, choose the appropriate device template, and enter the device name, agent, media and address information.

data.name: FundamentalsDeviceSecurity
data.value: Review the client and server addresses, authentication and security settings. Enter the credentials and keys required by the device.

data.name: FundamentalsDeviceSave
data.value: Save the device, open it from Devices, and read an object to check the connection. Review the device logs if the read fails.

data.name: FundamentalsScheduleDescription
data.value: Use a schedule to run device operations automatically.

data.name: FundamentalsScheduleCreate
data.value: Open Add schedule, give it a name, and set its execution time or recurrence.

data.name: FundamentalsScheduleTargets
data.value: Choose the devices and the operations or scripts that the schedule should run.

data.name: FundamentalsScheduleSave
data.value: Enable and save the schedule. Review the schedule logs after it runs to check the result.
